title: Closed discrete bases in countable-dimensional topological vector spaces: Lemma 2
author: Ol'ga Sipacheva
work: Closed discrete bases in countable-dimensional topological vector spaces
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma 2 (source0.tex lines 241--249, source label l2), that every countable-dimensional topological vector space over a finite field admits a continuous group norm and a basis that is discrete for it and either closed in the completion or with the origin as its only limit point, the space itself being incomplete for that norm, delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 251--345 (95 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The lemma is the finite-field case of the paper's main theorem on closed discrete bases and is the technical heart of the note: the proof constructs the norm by an explicit transfinite recursion over a basis, tracks the closure of the basis inside the completion through a Cauchy-sequence analysis, and separates the two alternatives (basis closed, or zero the only limit point) by a case analysis on the accumulating sequences; it invokes only the article's own preceding lemma and two classical references. H2: a complete original research-paper lemma with a long, fully written proof whose construction and case analysis are not qualifying-exam material.
